name: The Humane League: cage-free accountability campaigns, US and global (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: hens out of cages at companies THL pressed itself, 55% US by ACE's hens in the supply chains of the companies its US and global accountability programmes engaged (135 and 114 million); the rest spread by world population. A judgment.
summary: The Humane League's own cage-free accountability campaigns in the US and globally cost about $5.1 million in 2025 (ACE's 2024 programme costs in 2025 prices; THL UK's UK work is in the grants line and THL's running of the Open Wing Alliance in its other programmes). We credit them with a share of the 5.5 million hens that left cages in 2025 at companies THL pressed itself (its count of 7.5 million, less THL UK's and the Alliance members' switches, which the grants line credits), of which we judge 30% wouldn't have switched yet without the pressure. That share is THL's among the groups times this line's part of THL's own resources on the campaigns; the other-programmes model takes its grassroots mobilisation's part of the same pool, so no switch is credited twice. The count is THL's own and what the pressure brought forward a judgment, so the result is discounted for missing data, and past wins count at THL's own next-dollar figure. The result is below the site's animal-welfare median; the biggest uncertainties are how many switches the pressure brought forward and how THL's 2025 money splits between this line and its mobilisation.

Hens moved out of cages in 2025 under the commitments THL and the Alliance pressed

source.title: The Humane League, 2025 Annual Report (web version)
source.quote: 7.5M hens spared from cages around the globe

rows.explainer: THL's own count for 2025 (the printed report, p. 3, gives the same). Named switches: Subway in North America (nearly 340,000 hens) after the 2025 Eggsposé, The Cheesecake Factory (nearly 185,000).

rows.label: Of those, UK hens switched at companies THL UK pressed (credited in the grants line)
rows.explainer: Our judgment. THL's count is of hens at the companies it and the Alliance pressed, so its UK part is the switches at THL UK's engaged companies, not the whole country's change: ACE's sheet puts those companies' supply chains at 2.55 million hens, most already compliant. The high end is the UK's whole change in 2025 (82.7% against 78.6% cage-free of about 45 million hens, Our World in Data and the British Egg Information Service). THL UK is a separate charity THL funds by a grant, so these switches are credited in the grants line (as a share of the UK's whole change) and taken out here.

source.title: Open Wing Alliance, 2025 end-of-year review
source.quote: With direct outreach and oversight, the report helped secure 16 wins

rows.explainer: Companies that restored, re-dated or reported progress on stalled pledges after the alliance's outreach (REWE and Best Western among them).

rows.label: Hens a year still caged under each other accountability win
rows.explainer: Our judgment for the 15 wins besides REWE: the hens not yet cage-free under a stalled pledge that was restored or re-dated. The review's other named win, Best Western (hotels, about 30% of its eggs not yet cage-free), is far smaller than REWE; the 'six companies' that updated policies are mostly hospitality and food-service firms. The grants line's model's judgment.

rows.label: Of those, hens at companies Alliance members pressed (credited in the grants line)
rows.explainer: REWE's hens not yet cage-free and the other 15 wins of the Fair and Fowl report, the grants line's pool for the members' accountability wins, standing in for the year's switches at the companies they pressed (THL's count gives no split). Taken out here, as in the other-programmes model, so the same hens count in one pool only.

rows.label: Hens moved out of cages at companies THL pressed itself, 2025
rows.explainer: THL's 7.5 million less THL UK's and the Alliance members' switches: the pool this model and the other-programmes model's grassroots branch share. Observed switches are delivered already: no pledges-kept rate, and no division by years of pressure (templates.md, corporate-campaign accountability).

rows.label: Share of those switches from battery (not enriched) cages
rows.explainer: Our judgment, as in the other-programmes model: the hens taken out above (THL UK's and REWE's) are nearly all in enriched cages; the switches left at companies THL pressed itself are in the US and the multinationals' supply chains in Latin America and Asia, out of battery cages, with some European ones from enriched cages.

rows.label: SADs averted per hen-year out of a cage
rows.explainer: The shared figures for a hen moved from a battery cage (2024 SADs) or an enriched cage (2025 SADs) to an aviary, mixed by the share above. The species step converts the two versions separately.

rows.label: Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: The site's one answer to how many years a won pledge, law or rule counts before it would have come anyway (Your values → How impact is counted; docs/normalization.md 2.9). A switch brought forward counts the same years.

rows.label: Lag from the pressure to the switches it causes
rows.explainer: The lag between a year's pressure and the switches it brings (0-2 years, the template's recipe for accountability on observed switches).

rows.label: Discount for the lag
rows.explainer: The wait discounted at the shared rate, like every future benefit.

rows.label: Discounted years of impact
rows.explainer: Years counted, discounted at the shared rate from when the switch takes effect.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (how far the count can be trusted)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, as in the other-programmes model, about the validity of the count only (that the outcome isn't measured is the missing-data step): THL's 7.5 million hens spared is its own count and may include switches at companies it didn't press.

rows.label: Share of switches under pressed commitments that wouldn't have come yet without the pressure
rows.explainer: Our judgment, one question per switch: would it have come this year anyway? The anchor, pressed pledges kept at 92% (the Open Wing Alliance's tracker, 2025 Fair and Fowl report) against 77% for all due cage-free pledges (the site's shared rate), gives (0.92 - 0.77) / 0.92, about 0.16, for an average pressed pledge. The switches credited here come from companies that had stalled or gone silent (Subway, Walmart, Ahold Delhaize; REWE dropped its deadline), where pressure matters more than for a pledge already on track (THL UK's switches under passed UK deadlines take 0.2), so 0.3 (0.1-0.6). Each switch credited counts the shared years.

rows.label: Share of the switches that wouldn't have come yet
rows.explainer: The judgment above: what the pressure brought forward is the years counted, so this asks only whether the switch would have come this year anyway (Convention 5).

rows.label: THL's share of all groups' resources behind the switches at companies it pressed itself
rows.explainer: ACE's estimates for the same campaigns: other groups contribute 11% of THL's US and 15% of its global accountability work (5-20% by ACE's bounds), so THL's share, weighted by the two programmes' costs ($3.37 million US, $1.60 million global), is about 0.87; the low end, 0.7, allows for Alliance members' part in THL's global campaigns. The switches at companies Alliance members pressed and THL UK's are taken out of the pool, so what is left is THL's own campaigns.

rows.label: THL's grassroots mobilisation spending, 2025 (another line)
rows.explainer: The other-programmes model's figure for organising volunteers and supporters, protests, investigations and their communications: THL's programme spending less its grants, this line, its policy work, new commitments and the Open Wing Alliance's running (about $2.7 million; $1.0-3.5 million over that model's ranges). Its share of the resources behind the switches is credited there.

rows.label: All of THL's resources behind its own campaigns' switches
rows.explainer: The same resources the other-programmes model counts: this line's campaigns, the grassroots mobilisation and the volunteers' time.

rows.label: This line's share of the resources behind the switches
rows.explainer: Credit by share of resources (Convention 2): THL's share among the groups (ACE's estimates), times this line's share of THL's own resources on those campaigns. The other-programmes model takes the mobilisation's share of the same pool over the same total, and the volunteers' time is credited to no dollar, so together the two lines never get more than THL's share.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: This line's share of the resources behind the switches; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Share of commitments companies keep: none applied (observed switches)
rows.explainer: 1: the switches are hens already out of cages, an observed flow delivered already, so the shared rate of pledges kept doesn't apply (templates.md, corporate-campaign accountability).

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: The shared missing-data step (docs/normalization.md 2.12): nobody measured how many of these switches the pressure caused; the count is THL's own and what wouldn't have come yet is a judgment.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Side effect: wider gains from the switches, as a share of the hens' gain
rows.explainer: Our judgment. Pressed companies' switches push producers to convert barns that also supply buyers without a commitment, and make cage-free laws easier to pass. Range 0-30%.

rows.label: Side effect: caged eggs sold elsewhere and dearer eggs, as a share of the hens' gain
rows.explainer: Our judgment. When a buyer stops taking caged eggs, some of those eggs are sold to other buyers for a while, so fewer hens leave cages than the switch suggests; dearer cage-free eggs move a few buyers to chicken meat (more animals per calorie), while fewer eggs bought offsets part. A harm, so negative. Range 0 to -25%.

rows.label: Side effects, net, as a share of the hens' gain
rows.explainer: The two side effects above, each read through the side-effects slider.
